events.title: Death of Saint Patrick (traditional date)
events.description: Saint Patrick, the Romano-British missionary credited with spreading Christianity in Ireland, is traditionally held to have died on March 17, with the year commonly given as 461 though uncertain. His feast day is observed on this date.
events.significance: March 17 became St. Patrick's Day, celebrated worldwide as a feast day and a symbol of Irish culture and heritage.

events.title: British Evacuation of Boston
events.description: British forces under General William Howe evacuated Boston after months of siege by the Continental Army, aided by cannon brought from Fort Ticonderoga and placed on Dorchester Heights under George Washington's command.
events.significance: It was a major early American victory in the Revolutionary War, ending British control of Boston; the date is still commemorated as Evacuation Day in Massachusetts.

events.title: Proclamation of the Kingdom of Italy
events.description: The first Italian Parliament in Turin proclaimed Victor Emmanuel II King of Italy, uniting most of the peninsula under the House of Savoy.
events.significance: It marked the culmination of the main phase of the Risorgimento and the creation of a unified Italian national state.

events.title: Launch of Vanguard 1
events.description: The United States launched Vanguard 1, a small satellite that became the fourth artificial satellite in orbit and the first to use solar cells for power.
events.significance: Vanguard 1 is the oldest human-made object still in orbit and provided valuable data on Earth's shape and upper atmosphere density.

events.title: South African Apartheid Referendum
events.description: White South African voters approved a referendum by about 69 percent to support negotiations to end apartheid and establish a new constitution under President F. W. de Klerk.
events.significance: The result paved the way for multiracial elections in 1994 and the end of institutionalized white minority rule.
